commander_specific_hypothesis: Doctor Doom connives a Villain at the beginning of each combat. Glorious Purpose adds a +1/+1 counter to each creature that connives and a plan counter to itself; on its sixth plan counter it turns into a four-card burst that can cast spells for free.
oracle_rules_checked: PASS — Glorious Purpose, The Soul Stone and Doctor Doom current Oracle text directly checked
combo_prerequisites_verified: PASS — each creature connive event adds a plan counter; sixth counter sacrifices the Plan then exiles top four to cast spells free
official_legality_checked: PASS — current references confirm Glorious Purpose and The Soul Stone are Commander-legal
test_metric_and_success_threshold: No matched-seed test; qualitative gate: reward the commander’s guaranteed combat connive with a low-cost engine that has a clear six-trigger payoff.
baseline_result: Baseline includes The Soul Stone as a 2-mana black rock with a 7-mana harness/recursion activation.
variant_result: Variant adds Glorious Purpose, with plan counters from commander and other connive effects; Soul Stone removed.
sample_size_and_uncertainty: No empirical comparison; qualitative review only.
decision_reason_or_rejection_reason: ACCEPT. Two-mana plan that directly rewards the commander’s guaranteed combat connive and stacks with Kang, Leader, M.O.D.O.K., Baron Strucker and Lethal Scheme. Six plan counters exile the top four cards and allow any number of spells among them to be cast for free. The Soul Stone is cut because its mana-rock role is covered elsewhere and its recursion engine requires a seven-mana tap/exile activation; this is a deliberate long-game recursion versus commander-specific engine trade.
reviewer_notes: Candidate ranking is discovery evidence, not automatic inclusion.
